candidates.text: The States essentially want the Federal Judiciary to order the Executive Branch to alter its arrest policy so as to make more arrests
candidates.speaker: Kavanaugh, J., for the Court
phrases: want the Federal Judiciary to order the Executive Branch to alter its arrest policy
candidates.reason: States the Court's holding and rule: States lack standing to compel more arrests or prosecutions.

candidates.text: It bears emphasis that the question of whether the federal courts have jurisdiction under Article III is distinct from the question of whether the Executive Branch is complying
candidates.speaker: Kavanaugh, J., for the Court
phrases: the question of reviewability is different from the question of legality
candidates.reason: Defines the holding's narrowness (reviewability, not legality), which the brief stresses.

candidates.text: The States lack standing because federal courts do not have authority to redress their injuries
candidates.speaker: Gorsuch, J., concurring in the judgment
candidates.reason: Three-Justice redressability rationale and the universal-vacatur critique praised in the brief's Critique.

candidates.text: The majority's conception of Presidential authority smacks of the powers that English monarchs claimed prior to the `Glorious Revolution' of 1688
candidates.speaker: Alito, J., dissenting
phrases: smacks of the powers that English monarchs claimed
candidates.reason: The lone dissent's central charge, echoed by textualist critics.

candidates.text: The Court weaves together multiple doctrinal strands to create a rule that is not only novel, but also in tension with other decisions
candidates.speaker: Barrett, J., concurring in the judgment
candidates.reason: Doctrinal critique of the majority's reading of Linda R. S.
